decisions: alexei-led/ccgram rejected at sighting 3 rather than listed, resolving the Herdr-specificity question the 2026-08-29 audit deferred to this point. Opening it settled it: CCGram sits on top of a terminal multiplexer and names three interchangeable backends — tmux, Herdr, and agterm — so Herdr is a backend, not the purpose, and the project would be as useful with Herdr removed. The Herdr integration is real and deep (socket protocols 14-20, agent.list as the sole identity source, opaque herdr-session-v1 targets), which is why it survived two sightings, and it fails on specificity alone at 262 stars and MIT. Rejected alternative: listing it in Phone and mobile, where five Herdr-only clients already cover the ground.

'Remote and mobile' split into 'Remote access' and 'Phone and mobile' rather than retiring a healthy incumbent. The five promotions would have taken the section to 9 against a soft cap of 8, and the cap rule offers splitting or replacing; every incumbent still clears every bar, so retiring one to make room would have been churn. The split is functional — reaching a server from another computer, versus driving agents from a phone — and leaves both sections well under the cap.

jhochenbaum/herdr-hunk-diff listed despite the overlap flag against herdr-reviewr raised at sighting 1. They are close but not the same job: reviewr is a general review-and-file-viewer sidebar, hunk-diff is hunk-granular diff review with inline comments routed back to the authoring agent. Rejected alternative: replacing reviewr, which has 625 stars and is healthy on every measure. The section sits at 4 of 8, so both fit; re-examine if either stalls.

kryptamine/herdr-auto-title recorded as a candidate, not listed, even though at 84 stars and a same-day push it is stronger than the listed sh1ma/herdr-auto-title (53 stars, pushed 2026-08-13). Nothing skips probation. If it still qualifies in three weeks this becomes a replace-not-add decision, since the two do the same job under the same name.
audits.notes: Phase 5 weakest-entry review: fkiene/llmtrim-herdr, flagged for a first look on 2026-08-29, had crossed the liveness bar and was handled above, so the discretionary review moved to the next weakest incumbent. That is razajamil/herdr-plugin-workspace-manager (38 stars, pushed 16 days ago, MIT) — it clears every bar and would be admitted today, so no action. Worth noting for a future audit that Navigation and layout now holds three entries doing declarative workspace or session bootstrapping (herdr-spreader, herdr-sessionizer, herdr-plugin-workspace-manager, plus herdr-plugin-sesh as a picker); that is the section most likely to want a replace-not-add decision next. Rejected-with-license-missing recheck: pi-extensible-workflows (208 stars), herdr-tab-smart-rename (70), herdr-board (98), backpine/remote-agent-workspace (60, and now 74 days stale) are all still unlicensed; herdrm (665) likewise, and it is now the largest unlicensed miss, so the README header was updated to lead with it. yigitkonur/native-shortcuts-herd remains rejected at 112 days since last push. Two new rejects this run: tdi/herdr-worktree-setup (25 stars, genuinely Herdr-specific, no license) and apemost/dotfiles (25 stars, carries the herdr topic but the README does not mention Herdr once). The installed binary is 0.8.0 while the current release is 0.9.0, so no claim in this run's Trending items was checked against the binary — all three cite the release notes or the blog, which is the correct source for news.

Opened this run: CCGram is a Telegram bridge that sits on top of a terminal multiplexer and names three interchangeable backends — tmux, Herdr, and agterm — so Herdr is a backend rather than the purpose. The Herdr integration is genuinely deep (socket protocols 14-20, agent.list as the sole identity source, opaque herdr-session-v1 targets, `herdr integration install`), which is why it survived two sightings, but the project would be exactly as useful with Herdr removed. 262 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-05 — it fails on specificity alone, not traction. trending_policy: Trending items are exempt from the probation rule and are NOT sources: they are dated, sourced news items dropped after ~8 weeks or when superseded. A trending item never graduates into `sources` automatically — an entry must clear the normal bar on its own.

trending.text: v0.9.0 removes the single-process `--no-session` mode: every TUI launch now attaches to a background server, and `server stop` is what ends a session. Closing a primary workspace that has open worktree workspaces now needs explicit group intent (`workspace close --group`), and new lifecycle event subscriptions start with live events instead of replaying retained history — API and plugin clients must subscribe before taking their initial snapshot or they will miss changes.

v0.9.0: local and saved SSH machines now live in one window with a combined agent list and automatic reconnects (`herdr machine`), multiple clients can view different workspaces and tabs independently, the terminal UI moved into each client to cut redraw work in busy multi-client sessions, and Kitty graphics are on by default in compatible terminals.
Blog: 'Connecting the machines' — the 0.9 multi-machine client, why it took longer than expected, and Herdr Cloud named as what comes next.
Herdr joined Y Combinator (Fall 2026); runtime stays Apache-2.0. One-person team; YC page cites 25k stars and 340k downloads in four months.

v0.8.2: Windows support is now generally available on stable (previously preview-only); the plugin marketplace now discovers manifests at repository roots and subdirectories and groups multiple plugins per repository; Qwen Code state detection and native session restore.
Blog: 'Ten agents, three clients, 95% less CPU' — rendering and status-indicator work for running a fleet.

36,426 stars on 2026-09-08, up from 33,189 ten days earlier and ~15k in early July, when it hit #1 on GitHub Trending. The plugin marketplace held 1,033 repositories on the same date, up from 884; 60 of them clear this list's 25-star bar, up from 50.
No company publicly documented as running Herdr in production could be found. Standing search target.
